boundary: Post-vote workshops. Public historical context is available to both roles. Private instructions and all four candidate packages are fictional. A workshop action establishes no official vote, authority or commitment.

public_evidence.location: page 2, chair's draft introduction and decision
public_evidence.text: The Security Council unanimously adopted draft S/2023/378 as resolution 2682 (2023), with all 15 members in favour. The meeting record contains no separate national explanation from France or the United Kingdom.

The resolution extended UNAMI's existing mandate until 31 May 2024. It separately requested an independent strategic review by 31 March 2024 and consultation with Iraq and other identified stakeholders. The review deadline was not the mandate expiry.

Recommend a future change shortening the mandate term. Add a confidential consultation annex and a public aggregate summary.

required_content.action: Keep the review deadline separate from the mandate expiry. Describe the operative package and any future change it would require, or which terms preclude a package.
required_content.positions: Attribute each private workshop condition to its own role and distinguish it from any real national explanation.
required_content.open_issues: Identify consultation documentation as a workshop choice and keep unresolved workshop constraints explicit.
required_content.authority: Treat the two deadlines and the requested review as historical. Treat any new confidential annex or shorter term as a proposal requiring the relevant authorization.

public_evidence.location: first and second roll calls and chair's declarations
public_evidence.text: On Brazil and Switzerland's nine-month draft S/2023/506, Brazil and the United Kingdom voted yes. The draft failed 13–1–1 because Russia, a permanent member, voted no. The separate six-month draft S/2023/507 failed 2–3–10 for lack of sufficient affirmative votes. Brazil abstained and the United Kingdom voted no on the second draft.
The nine-month proposal concerned renewal of cross-border authorization for humanitarian relief and the monitoring mechanism. It was a draft and the vote did not extend the authorization.

packages.text: Recommend nine months, with access through cross-border and cross-line channels and ordinary reporting.
Recommend nine months with both access modalities and an extra formal review checkpoint.
Recommend six months with both access modalities and an extra formal review checkpoint.
Recommend six months with both access modalities and ordinary reporting.

required_content.disposition: Distinguish failure of the two real drafts from the workshop result. Report a compatible workshop package or an explicit impasse.
required_content.action: State the proposed duration and oversight for a supported package, or explain the blocking conflict. Keep access modalities and authority distinct.
required_content.positions: Preserve Brazil's and the UK's different recorded votes across the instruments, and attribute both private instructions to their respective workshop roles.
required_content.open_issues: Explain the materially unresolved condition or the specific overlap. Distinguish a preference about oversight from the historical reason a draft failed.
required_content.authority: The 13 affirmative votes did not renew authorization. A workshop recommendation does not establish a new official vote or authorize cross-border action.
